notes:
The 8th Grade problem

Cause: “Students are under” was set to /StudentAccounts/Middle School, which is one school. With school level 1, the next level down is the grade, so {school} became “8th Grade”. The example line made up a path instead of using a real one, so it hid the problem.
Fix: when the level right under “Students are under” is a grade, GAMbit treats “Students are under” itself as the school. That setup now goes to /Chrome Devices/Hancock Middle School. Graduation years and former or suspended student org units are handled the same way. The Assignment sync tab uses the same rule.
Example line: it now shows real org units from your district and where each would move.
New warning: if “Students are under” looks like a single school, it says only that school’s students will be used and suggests /StudentAccounts.
My suggestion: set “Students are under” to /StudentAccounts so every school is covered at once. In my test with your layout, a Middle School 8th grader went to /Chrome Devices/Hancock Middle School and a High School 10th grader to /Chrome Devices/Hancock High School.
Name mismatches: if a school’s Chromebook org unit is named differently from its student org unit, like “HMS”, choose the org unit map instead of a pattern. The pattern can only match identical names.

Custom time and days

Run the move on a schedule: pick a time and tick days Mon–Sun, or use the Weekdays and Every day buttons. Then click Save & schedule, or Turn off to stop it. The line underneath confirms the schedule, for example “On: Mon, Wed, Fri at 6:30 AM, for every Chromebook.”
Run the assigned-user jobs on a schedule: the same time and day picker, for blanking unused Chromebooks and setting assigned users. The Schedule… button in the “Set it to the last signed-in user” section takes you there.
Choosing all seven days runs it daily; anything else runs only on the days you ticked.
